title: Deep Ink Folio — NeurIPS Conference Manuscript
description: A NeurIPS/ICML-faithful two-column slide that mimics a typeset LaTeX article: justified serif body, a properly numbered display equation, and a results figure inset — all above a 9pt author-affiliation block.
philosophy: This template refuses the visual vocabulary of corporate decks entirely — no gradient heroes, no icon grids, no pull-quote typography. It exists for researchers who want their slides to read like the paper itself: rigorous, dense, and self-contained. The two-column justified layout enforces informational parity between methodology and results, and every typographic decision defers to the conventions of IEEE and NeurIPS proceedings. It is built for conference rooms where the audience reads while you speak, not audiences who need to be sold.
goodFor: ML/AI conference poster sessions (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR)
Methodology slides containing numbered display equations
Results-summary slides with a single small embedded figure
Academic journal club and lab-meeting presentations
avoidFor: Investor pitch decks or sales-oriented presentations
Visual-first brand storytelling with full-bleed imagery
Keynote talks requiring large hero graphics or animation
Informal standup or sprint-review team updates
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel indistinguishable from the opening page of a typeset NeurIPS proceedings manuscript — austere, rigorous, and deliberately pre-digital in its restraint. Compositional authority is established entirely through scale contrast and a single ruled divider; there is no color drama, no illustrative imagery, and no decorative hierarchy. The overall mood is monastic academic formality: a document that earns attention through density and precision, not visual seduction. Avoid any element that reads as 'designed' rather than 'typeset'.

examples.layoutNotes: Full live-area single-column centered layout with ~10% symmetrical outer margins; the paper title spans the full text-width in the upper third, separated from the author block below by a single thin rule line. Authors are arranged in a centered, horizontally distributed cluster with superscript affiliation markers, followed immediately by a compressed affiliation-and-email line. A small conference/venue label is set flush-right in the top margin gutter, mimicking proceedings headers. No decorative elements occupy the bottom third — it remains open as compositional breath.

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a page extracted directly from a NeurIPS proceedings PDF — dense, rigorous, and typographically austere in the tradition of LaTeX-set academic manuscripts. Compositional rhythm is bilaterally symmetric and column-balanced; hierarchy emerges purely from weight contrast and the spatial pause that surrounds the display equation, not from decorative intervention. The inset figure functions as evidence rather than ornamentation — small, precise, and subordinate to the prose. Resist every corporate-deck impulse: no gradient washes, no icon grids, no generous breathing room deployed for visual comfort rather than informational necessity.

    <text x="154" y="128" font-size="34" font-weight="700">Variational Sparse Attention with Learned Routing Priors</text>
  </g>
  <line x1="154" y1="152" x2="1766" y2="152" stroke="#1f2a36" stroke-width="1.2"/>
  <text x="1766" y="88" font-family="ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#8a9aa8" text-anchor="end" letter-spacing="2">NeurIPS 2026 — PRE-PROCEEDINGS DRAFT</text>

  <!-- LEFT COLUMN -->
  <g font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" fill="#1f2a36">
    <text x="154" y="210" font-size="18" font-weight="700" letter-spacing="1.2">3.1   FORMULATION</text>

    <!-- Justified body paragraph 1 -->
    <g font-size="17.5">
      <text x="154" y="252">Let <tspan font-style="italic">X</tspan> ∈ ℝ<tspan font-size="12" dy="-6">n×d</tspan><tspan dy="6"> denote the input sequence of </tspan><tspan font-style="italic">n</tspan> tokens embedded in ℝ<tspan font-size="12" dy="-6">d</tspan><tspan dy="6">. The canonical attention</tspan></text>
      <text x="154" y="278">operator incurs Θ(<tspan font-style="italic">n</tspan><tspan font-size="12" dy="-6">2</tspan><tspan dy="6">) memory, which is prohibitive for </tspan><tspan font-style="italic">n</tspan> ≥ 2<tspan font-size="12" dy="-6">14</tspan><tspan dy="6">. We relax the dense</tspan></text>
      <text x="154" y="304">coupling by introducing a latent routing variable <tspan font-style="italic">z</tspan><tspan font-size="12" dy="-6">ij</tspan><tspan dy="6"> ∈ {0, 1} that gates pairwise</tspan></text>
      <text x="154" y="330">interactions, and place a structured Bernoulli prior <tspan font-style="italic">p</tspan>(<tspan font-style="italic">z</tspan>) whose mean parameter</text>
      <text x="154" y="356">is tied to a low-rank content similarity estimator. The resulting evidence lower</text>
      <text x="154" y="382">bound admits the following stationary point, obtained by differentiating the free</text>
      <text x="154" y="408">energy with respect to the variational posterior <tspan font-style="italic">q</tspan><tspan font-size="12" dy="-6">φ</tspan><tspan dy="6">(</tspan><tspan font-style="italic">z</tspan> | <tspan font-style="italic">X</tspan>):</text>
    </g>

    <!-- Display equation -->
    <g font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" fill="#1f2a36">
      <text x="510" y="478" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle">
        <tspan font-style="italic">ℒ</tspan>(<tspan font-style="italic">θ</tspan>, <tspan font-style="italic">φ</tspan>) = 𝔼<tspan font-size="14" dy="4">q</tspan><tspan dy="-4">[ log </tspan><tspan font-style="italic">p</tspan><tspan font-size="14" dy="4">θ</tspan><tspan dy="-4">(</tspan><tspan font-style="italic">X</tspan> | <tspan font-style="italic">z</tspan>) ] − β · KL( <tspan font-style="italic">q</tspan><tspan font-size="14" dy="4">φ</tspan><tspan dy="-4"> ‖ </tspan><tspan font-style="italic">p</tspan> )</text>
      <text x="880" y="478" font-size="17" fill="#8a9aa8" text-anchor="end">(1)</text>
    </g>

    <!-- Body paragraph 2 -->
    <g font-size="17.5">
      <text x="154" y="548">where <tspan font-style="italic">β</tspan> ∈ [0, 1] trades reconstruction fidelity against routing sparsity. In practice</text>
      <text x="154" y="574">we anneal <tspan font-style="italic">β</tspan> along a cosine schedule from 0.02 to 0.4 over the first 5 000 steps,</text>
      <text x="154" y="600">which we empirically find to stabilise the Gumbel-softmax relaxation used to</text>
      <text x="154" y="626">backpropagate through the discrete gates. The expected FLOP budget per layer</text>
      <text x="154" y="652">reduces to Θ(<tspan font-style="italic">n</tspan> log <tspan font-style="italic">n</tspan>) once <tspan font-style="italic">β</tspan> saturates, matching the asymptotics reported by</text>
      <text x="154" y="678">Chen et al. (2024) while preserving full-rank gradients at the dense warm-up.</text>
    </g>

    <text x="154" y="726" font-size="18" font-weight="700" letter-spacing="1.2" font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" fill="#1f2a36">3.2   OPTIMISATION</text>
    <g font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" fill="#1f2a36" font-size="17.5">
      <text x="154" y="760">We optimise (1) with AdamW (<tspan font-style="italic">η</tspan> = 3×10<tspan font-size="12" dy="-6">−4</tspan><tspan dy="6">, weight decay 0.01), clipping gradients</tspan></text>
      <text x="154" y="786">at ‖<tspan font-style="italic">g</tspan>‖<tspan font-size="12" dy="-6">2</tspan><tspan dy="6"> ≤ 1.0. Mixed-precision (bf16) is used throughout; router logits are kept in</tspan></text>
      <text x="154" y="812">fp32 to avoid the saturation failure mode documented in Appendix B.3.</text>
    </g>
